sourceFingerprint.pageMapping: Printed body page N = physical PDF page N+26. Relevant page labels were checked against extraction headers and index; original figure renders inspected.

method: Read every assigned record including clinical and nested route notes against the original-book extraction, verified printed/PDF labels, visually inspected original Figures 5.11, 10.8 and 14.21, and cross-validated each correction with public primary anatomy or clinical research. Report text paraphrases source evidence; no textbook text/figure is copied into the repository.

perRecordAssessments.name: Internal carotid artery
perRecordAssessments.reason: Retain the cavernous cranial-nerve relationships, segment simplification, independent AChA origin, and collateral/fetal-PCA qualifications. The range of cortical and retinal ischaemic outcomes is appropriately conditional.

perRecordAssessments.name: Basilar artery
perRecordAssessments.reason: Retain prepontine/ventral pontine course and variable pontine/apical territories; locked-in and tegmental outcomes are conditional. The corticospinal linked record includes the supraspinal pathway, so its historical lateral-tract ID is not evidence that the basilar artery perfuses spinal cord. Interpeduncular-fossa link is a coarse regional landmark, not a perfused CSF compartment.

perRecordAssessments.name: Posterior cerebral artery
perRecordAssessments.reason: Retain cortical versus deep-branch separation, medial/inferior temporal-occipital supply, conditional macular sparing, and bilateral-thalamic Percheron variant. Calcarine is one cortical branch, not an alias for the whole PCA. Tuberothalamic syndrome linkage can reflect replacement of absent polar supply by paramedian branches, so no universal exclusive mapping is claimed.

findings.title: MCA connection list mixes its origin, own branches, and an ICA sibling

targets.original: Internal carotid artery (vasc-internal-carotid-artery) at the carotid bifurcation
targets.proposed: Internal carotid artery (vasc-internal-carotid-artery) at its intracranial terminal bifurcation

original: Lateral lenticulostriate perforators (vasc-lenticulostriate-arteries) from M1 — the deep supply to the putamen, caudate and internal capsule
Orbitofrontal and temporopolar branches, anterior temporal branches, insular (M2) branches, and the superior and inferior division trunks that fan out over the convexity
The anterior choroidal artery (vasc-anterior-choroidal-artery) arises nearby from the internal carotid and shares the deep territory
proposed: Lateral lenticulostriate perforators (vasc-lenticulostriate-arteries) from M1 — the deep supply to the putamen, caudate and internal capsule
Orbitofrontal and temporopolar branches, anterior temporal branches, insular (M2) branches, and the superior and inferior division trunks that fan out over the convexity

findings.explanation: Carotid bifurcation alone conventionally denotes the cervical common-carotid split and can misplace the MCA origin. The usual anterior choroidal artery arises independently from the supraclinoid ICA; it is not a downstream MCA branch. Its neighbouring and overlapping territory can be described separately without listing it as an MCA efferent.

findings.title: Vertebral artery muscular/radicular branches are listed as inflow

original: Subclavian artery (the first branch of the subclavian on each side) — the inflow of the posterior circulation
Muscular and radicular branches along the cervical course
proposed: Usually the proximal subclavian artery; vertebral origin variants occur

original: Posterior inferior cerebellar artery (vasc-posterior-inferior-cerebellar-artery) — the largest branch, supplying the lateral medulla and inferior cerebellum

proposed: Posterior inferior cerebellar artery (vasc-posterior-inferior-cerebellar-artery) — the largest branch, supplying the lateral medulla and inferior cerebellum
Anterior spinal artery (the paired ventral branches that join in the midline) and small posterior spinal/paramedian medullary perforators
Basilar artery (vasc-basilar-artery) — formed by the union of the two vertebral arteries at the pontomedullary junction

findings.title: Nested M2 note confuses the insular and opercular surfaces

targets.original: The insular (M2) segment runs in the Sylvian fissure over the insula, i.e. in the subarachnoid space on the opercular surface of the committed hemisphere envelope. Its distal (opercular) end is projected onto that envelope; the proximal two waypoints are literal vertices of the committed M2 mesh.
targets.proposed: The M2 segment courses in the Sylvian fissure over the insular surface. At the peri-insular sulci it continues into M3 branches over the opercula. The committed hemisphere envelope is a schematic display constraint and does not independently validate these local surfaces or the segment transition.

findings.explanation: The card function correctly distinguishes M2 and M3, but the nested course note calls the M2 route an opercular-surface course. Microscopic dissection distinguishes M2 on the insula from M3 along the medial opercular surfaces.

findings.title: Nested thalamogeniculate note borrows the paramedian entry route

targets.original: Intraparenchymal perforators: they arise from the P2 segment in the ambient cistern, pierce the posterior perforated substance and the lateral surface of the thalamus, and run inside the diencephalon. No envelope is declared because projecting them onto one would be anatomically wrong; their cisternal origin is the committed P2 vertex.
targets.proposed: Thalamogeniculate perforators usually arise from PCA P2 in the crural or ambient region and penetrate the geniculate/pulvinar region to reach inferolateral thalamic tissue. They are distinct from the paramedian P1 thalamoperforators entering the posterior perforated substance. The stored intraparenchymal route is schematic and does not validate individual entry sites or branching.

findings.explanation: The current note combines P2 origin with the posterior-perforated-substance entry of the medial P1 group. The primary study of 30 hemispheres describes variable P2/P3 origins and penetration of the geniculate bodies and pulvinar, rather than a universal medial entry through the posterior perforated substance.

findings.explanation: The lateral/hemispheric SCA record describes a distal cerebellar branch, while Nothnagel requires dorsal midbrain ocular-motor/cerebellar-output involvement. SCA trunk perforators can reach the midbrain, but this does not establish that this distal model branch supplies that syndrome. The telovelotonsillar PICA record describes cerebellar and fourth-plexus branches; it should not directly identify lateral-medullary supply normally dependent on proximal medullary perforators. Remove these specific reverse mappings while retaining general cerebellar syndromes and the parent artery records.

findings.title: Nested lateral-striate note contains an inconsistent unit conversion

targets.original: Intraparenchymal perforators: the group pierces the anterior perforated substance and runs INSIDE the brain, so no cortical envelope is declared. The single projected constraint is the entry point (0.018 au = 0.61 mm from ctx-hemisphere-l); the arborisation apex deliberately grazes the putamen surface, because a perforator ends in the structure it supplies.
targets.proposed: Lateral striate perforators pierce the anterior perforated substance and run within deep cerebral tissue. The stored entry projection and terminal anchors are construction choices in the atlas frame; they do not establish vessel termination, individual branching, or measured anatomical accuracy.

findings.explanation: The note reports 0.018 atlas units as 0.61 mm, inconsistent with the nearby 1.2 mm-per-unit examples (0.018 x 1.2 is 0.0216 mm). It also treats touching the putaminal surface as evidence of biological perforator termination, although perforators enter and arborize within tissue. Remove that numerical claim and preserve a plain schematic limitation rather than fabricating corrected anatomical measurements.

findings.title: Built-in vessel-course fallback retains stale group and choroidal text

targets.original: Medial lenticulostriate arteries (recurrent artery of Heubner)
targets.proposed: Medial striate arteries (including recurrent artery of Heubner)

original: medial group of the lenticulostriate arteries
proposed: medial group of the lenticulostriate arteries

targets.original: Arterial blood (oxygenated) — the largest medial perforator of the ACA
targets.proposed: Arterial blood (oxygenated) — medial ACA striate perforators, including Heubner

targets.original: Medial lenticulostriate arteries (recurrent artery of Heubner)
targets.proposed: ACA medial striate branches, including the recurrent artery of Heubner

targets.original: The cisternal segment hugs the committed `ctx-midbrain-surface` envelope (the same surface the three SCA courses declare): its middle waypoint is a literal vertex of it, 0.000 au from the surface. The TERMINAL is the opposite relation — a choroidal artery ends ON the plexus — so it is a deliberate graze on the committed `ctx-choroid-plexus-l` mesh (a literal plexus vertex), 12.664 au (15.20 mm) from the P2 take-off, which is the cisternal + choroidal-fissure interval the path crosses.
targets.proposed: Spatial route withheld. The former lateral-ventricular plexus endpoint does not establish a medial posterior choroidal course to the third-ventricular tela choroidea. Source-backed placement is required; the retained waypoints and construction distances do not validate arterial anatomy.

findings.explanation: The built-in fallback duplicates medial-group prose and still calls its modality one largest vessel, even though the record represents the group. Its medial-posterior-choroidal surface note certifies the old lateral-plexus terminal despite meshes:false and an anchor note already acknowledging the invalid course. Synchronize the group text and withheld-route limitation. Do not re-enable that mesh or adjust its coordinates.

duplicateAuthoredTablesReviewed.assessment: Fallback card functions, targets, territory links and clinical paragraphs generally match JSON; residual label/modality/choroidal surface note differences are VASC-R-010. No waypoint changes or anatomy certification recommended.

retainedLimitations: Textbook diagrams and public cadaveric samples support relative anatomy, not stereotaxic validation of this atlas, a universal vascular map, or patient stroke prediction.

Major cortical/deep arteries have overlapping and variable territories. Links indicate partial regional supply. Child vessel numbers, calibre and geometric endpoint contacts do not establish branch identity or an anatomical distribution.

Card clinical patterns are conditional; eponym boundaries vary and complete named syndromes are neither necessary nor guaranteed. SCA perforators may supply some dorsal/lateral midbrain tissue, and this does not validate the distal lateral-branch Nothnagel link.

Eight ventricular records correctly distinguish CSF spaces/openings from surrounding neural tissue and choroid plexus. Their arterial/venous descriptions refer to wall or plexal tissue, not a cavity that can infarct.
Medial posterior choroidal, pontine-perforator and certain other withheld meshes remain withheld. No invented replacement routes, coordinates, voxel territories or meshes are proposed.

Haines citation page ranges were not independently certified in this assignment because the assigned source was Blumenfeld. Existing PubMed links 6689705, 7070615, 33836500, 7985576 and 20692674 match their named research. Broad textbook references support gross concepts but do not validate every small branch statement.

Pericallosal/ACA and segment nomenclature varies. A2/A3/A4/A5 labels cannot be treated as a universal branch-name equivalence. Current callosomarginal/frontopolar function text explicitly preserves variable origins; no rigid segment-remapping is proposed.
No app files, git state, deployments, medical-result files, or memories were modified by this audit. Private figure renders and this report are outside the Git repository.

noChangeDecisions.decision: Retain ventricular flow and neighbouring anatomy
noChangeDecisions.reason: Book pp.132-137 and 215-216 support the cavity arrangement and flow; pp.155-157 support variable hydrocephalus mechanisms. Additional direct MRI-pathology/clinical series validate the current temporal-horn and neurocytoma corrections.

noChangeDecisions.decision: Retain cortical visual field and alexia distinctions
noChangeDecisions.reason: Book pp.474-475 and 894-896 support upper-bank lower-field loss, temporal Meyer-loop upper-field loss, dominant angular alexia-with-agraphia, and combined occipital-splenial pure alexia. Current wording is qualified.
Current prose avoids obligatory complete syndrome, fixed universal collateral adequacy and fixed branch counts. Exact biological supply cannot be inferred from a model tube.

noChangeDecisions.reason: The current linked CST card includes its supraspinal course, so lateral-CST ID is not evidence of spinal perfusion by basilar. Surface-root/fossa links are coarse relations to nearby supplied tissue, not full CSF or nerve territories; no metric certification is made.
